body.statement: Under the premises of \(\texttt{thm:exact-once-output-sensitive-enumeration}\), suppose every entry of the rational input \(\mathcal O_G\) has binary encoding length at most \(L_{\mathrm{bits}}\). The fraction-free immutable-row implementation of \(\operatorname{Enum}_G\), including common-ancestry computation, has deterministic total bit-operation time and bit storage polynomial in \(p\), \(m\), \(L_{\mathrm{bits}}\), \(2^p\), \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\), and the total emitted encoding length. Canonically reduced determinant-ratio certificates decide equality of interned rows. Thus no superpolynomial intermediate or certificate growth is forced in this rational published-class regime.
body.proof_tex:
Write every rational input coordinate in lowest terms with positive
denominator. For one principal regression solve, multiply its coefficient
matrix and right-hand side by the product \(d\) of the denominators of the
at most \((p+1)^2\) entries in the augmented matrix. If every input
numerator and denominator has at most \(L_{\mathrm{bits}}\) binary digits,
then
\[
 \operatorname{bits}(d)\le(p+1)^2L_{\mathrm{bits}},
 \qquad \operatorname{bits}(dx)=O(p^2L_{\mathrm{bits}})
 \tag{28}
\]
for every scaled entry \(dx\). Scaling the entire augmented system by the
same positive integer leaves its solution unchanged. By
\(\texttt{lem:original-row-invariance}\), every principal within-view
covariance matrix is positive definite. Its leading principal minors in
any fixed ordering of \(A\) are therefore positive, so the no-pivot
fraction-free recurrence has no zero pivot.

The cited \(\texttt{lem:bareiss-minor-growth}\) gives exact integer division
and represents every transformed coefficient as a signed bordered minor of
the scaled augmented matrix. If a \(k\times k\) integer matrix \(K\) has
entries of magnitude below \(2^h\), the Leibniz formula gives
\[
 |\det K|
 \le\sum_{\sigma\in\mathfrak S_k}
 \prod_{i=1}^k|K_{i,\sigma(i)}|
 <k!\,2^{kh}.
\]
Consequently, using (28) and \(k\le p+1\),
\[
 \operatorname{bits}(\det K)
 \le kh+\lceil\log_2(k!)\rceil+1
 =O\!\left(p^3L_{\mathrm{bits}}+p\log p\right).
 \tag{29}
\]
The adjugate identity for the nonsingular principal covariance matrix
expresses every regression coordinate as a bordered-minor numerator divided
by its determinant. Reducing by the greatest common divisor and choosing a
positive denominator gives a canonical determinant-ratio certificate of
the bit length in (29). Two rational coordinates are equal exactly when
their canonical numerator-denominator pairs are equal, and two interned
rows are equal exactly when all their coordinate certificates agree.

The ordered exact-real proof of
\(\texttt{thm:exact-once-output-sensitive-enumeration}\) performs a number
of field operations and comparisons polynomial in \(p\), \(m\), \(2^p\),
and \(N_{\mathrm{out}}\). By (28)--(29), rational addition,
multiplication, division, sign comparison, and equality comparison act on
operands of polynomial binary length. Grade-school integer arithmetic is
polynomial in operand length. Euclid's algorithm is also polynomial: after
at most two remainder steps its positive second operand is less than half
its earlier value, so \(h\)-bit inputs require at most \(2h+1\) remainder
steps, each on operands of at most \(h\) bits. Fragment keys contain \(p\)
integer identifiers of \(O(p)\) bits and introduce no rational-expression
growth. Exact support tests for common ancestry compare canonical
numerators with zero and therefore have the same polynomial cost.

Multiplying these polynomial per-operation costs by the operation counts of
the exact-real theorem, then adding the total emitted encoding length,
proves the asserted polynomial bit time. Multiplying the height bound (29)
by the stored row and output counts, and adding the integer tries and the
\(p\times p\) Boolean ancestry accumulator, proves polynomial bit storage.
Every row is computed directly from an original principal covariance system,
so its height bound is not recursively iterated through the \(2^p\) subset
states. This proves that no superpolynomial intermediate or certificate
growth is forced in the stated rational regime.
body.justification: The retained resolved theorem ID lifts the full-lattice exact-real result, including ancestry zero tests, to deterministic output-polynomial bit complexity.
body.gap: Bareiss elimination controls one solve but does not itself account simultaneously for every subset regression, canonical row certificate, fragment key, emitted tuple, and ancestry intersection.
body.consumer: Exact symbolic implementations can advertise polynomial bit complexity in the explicit lattice size and numerical output size.
